requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
I found no gaps. I did not run the tests; the judgment rests on reading the implementation and the test assertions.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**
- **Command form.** The syntax and the alias come from the clap `Command::Author` definition in `src/main.rs`. It declares `alias = "author-evidence"`, `--config`, `--stdout`, `-v/--verbose`, and `--missing` and `--force`. `--missing` conflicts with `--force` and with `--stdout`.
- **Author one existing subject under refresh.**
  - `main` (the `Command::Author` arm) calls `author_evidence_with_options`. That function skips a current subject under `--missing` through `batch::subject_is_current`, and it treats `--stdout` as `--force`.
  - `AssessmentSources::prepare` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs` returns a "no matching requirement or named example" error for an unknown subject or a term. It treats requirements and examples alike.
  - `AuthoringSubject::parse` and `configured_assessment` do the rest, and `configured_assessment` writes the evidence file.
- **Report subject, backend, model, evidence destination and usage path.**
  - `AuthoringOutcome` carries all five values.
  - `configured_assessment` fills them in, and `main` prints them as `"{subject}: {backend} / {model}; policy …"`, then `Evidence: <path>` and `Usage: <path>`.
- **Evidence destination is the file path by default, or stdout with `--stdout`.** `main` prints `outcome.evidence_path` when it is `Some`. In stdout mode it prints `Evidence: stdout`, because `configured_assessment` sets `evidence_path` to `None`.
- **Stdout mode sends the completion report and diagnostics to stderr.**
  - `main` uses `eprintln!` for the report in stdout mode. It also uses `eprintln!` for the "false" notice and the verbose rationale.
  - Errors propagate through `main`'s `Result`, which is reported on stderr.
  - The only stdout writes during assessment are the evidence JSON in `configured_assessment`.
  - The `println!` calls in `BatchProgress` go to stderr.

**Tests**
- **Default report and alias.** `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free` runs `author-evidence` and asserts the stdout starts with `SUBJECT: ollama / MODEL`. It also checks that `Evidence:` ends in `evidence/<subject>.json` and resolves to the real file, and that `Usage:` appears.
- **Stdout mode.**
  - `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files` asserts that stdout parses as pure JSON.
  - The same test asserts that stderr contains the subject and backend line, `Evidence: stdout`, and `Usage:`.
  - It also asserts that stderr contains the "false" notice and the verbose rationale, and that no evidence file is written.
- **Verbose.** `verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs` covers `-v` and `--verbose`.
- **Unknown subject.** `author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets` asserts a failure naming the unknown subject.
- **Refresh flags.**
  - `missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject` covers `--missing` as the default.
  - It checks that `--missing` keeps a current record without reading the (broken) configuration.
  - It checks that `--missing` and `--force` are mutually exclusive, and that `--stdout` conflicts with `--missing`.
  - It checks that `--force` and `--stdout` reassess, and that `author-evidence` works on a named example.
- **Config selection.** `--config` is exercised through `Fixture::run` and the `configuration_precedence` tests that use it. `authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file` covers configuration resolution.

All behavior in the implementation is specified by this requirement, `refresh`, or other requirements the same code marks with `{impl}`.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
